When will I use this?

Formulae: when will I use this?

Whenever a rule turns the numbers you know into the one you need.

Maintenance electrician

Engineering and manufacturing

\(\displaystyle I = \dfrac{P}{V}\)

3 A or 13 A fuse for a toaster?

A plug fuse must be big enough for the appliance's current. Current = power ÷ voltage, I = P ÷ V. UK mains is 230 V.

  1. Toaster, 2000 W: I = \(2000 \div 230 = 8.7\) A, too much for a 3 A fuse, so 13 A.
  2. Lamp, 60 W: I = \(60 \div 230 = 0.26\) A, so a 3 A fuse is fine.

The answer: \(2000 \div 230 = 8.7\) A
